issues.span: 道は言はしずか、名は言はしずか
issues.advice: The opening 道可道非常道 / 名可名非常名 means 'the Dao that can be spoken is not the constant Dao; the name that can be named is not the constant name.' The translation renders it as 'the Dao is quiet/wordless,' losing the conditional 'can be spoken/named' and the 'not the constant' negation entirely.

issues.span: 常無を欲して妙を観ず。常有を欲して徼を観ず
issues.advice: 常無欲以觀其妙 / 常有欲以觀其徼 means 'constantly without desire, one observes its mystery; constantly with desire, one observes its manifestations.' The translation misparses 常無/常有 as objects of 欲 and drops the 'constantly' (常) modifier and the contrast of 妙 vs 徼.

issues.span: 此二者は同一の源から異名なり
issues.advice: 此兩者同出而異名 means 'these two emerge together but are named differently' — the translation adds 'source' (源) not present and weakens 同出; should express 'same origin, different names' more faithfully.

issues.span: 玄を繰り返す
issues.advice: 玄之又玄 means 'mystery upon mystery' / 'the deepest mystery,' not 'repeat the mystery.' The reduplicative 又玄 intensifies, it does not mean repetition.

issues.span: 万物的母
issues.advice: 有名萬物之母 means 'the named is the mother of the ten thousand things.' '万物的母' is ungrammatical Japanese and mistranslates 萬物 (myriad things) as a modifier; should be '万物の母'.

issues.span: façonner la pointe et ne pas la laisser croître n'est pas aussi bon que cesser
issues.advice: The source 揣而銳之不可長保 means 'if you hammer it sharp, it cannot be preserved for long' — not a comparison with 'cesser'. The repeated 'n'est pas aussi bon que cesser' is a mistranslation applied to clauses that do not contain 不如其已.

issues.span: garder les or et l'argent dans un hall plein n'est pas aussi bon que cesser

issues.span: garder la richesse et la gloire avec orgueil et se laisser porter la faute n'est pas aussi bon que cesser
issues.advice: 富貴而驕自遺其咎 means 'wealth and honor with arrogance bring self-inflicted blame' — not a comparison with ceasing.

issues.span: faire subir un désastre à soi-même n'est pas aussi bon que cesser
issues.advice: This clause is a spurious duplication; 自遺其咎 was already rendered above. Remove the invented repetition.

issues.span: accomplir la réussite de la gloire et de la renommée n'est pas aussi bon que cesser
issues.advice: 功成名遂 means 'when the work is done and the name is made' — a temporal clause, not a comparison with ceasing.

issues.span: se retirer de la vie n'est pas aussi bon que cesser
issues.advice: 身退 means 'withdraw the self / retire from position', not 'se retirer de la vie' (withdraw from life). Also it is not a comparison with ceasing.

issues.span: n'est pas aussi bon que cesser
issues.advice: The phrase is mechanically repeated seven times, producing incoherent and ungrammatical French. Only the first clause (持而盈之不如其已) warrants this comparison.

issues.span: les or et l'argent
issues.advice: 金玉 should be rendered 'or et jade'; 'argent' is a mistranslation of 玉.

issues.span: se retirer de la vie
issues.advice: This misrepresents the Daoist idea of 身退 (retiring from office/merit), suggesting death or renunciation of life.

payload.translation: 持ちて満しむるは如し已に、揣て鋭しむるは長保せず、金玉を満てた室は守れず、富貴を誇り自棄にして咎を遺すなり。功成名遂にして身退す。天の道なり。

issues.span: 持ちて満しむるは如し已に
issues.advice: 「不如其已」は「それ已むに如かず」の意。原文の比較構文「不如」を「如し」と訳すと意味が逆転するので、「已むに如かず」と訳す。

issues.span: 揣て鋭しむるは長保せず
issues.advice: 原文は「不可長保」（長く保つべからず）。「長保せず」は意味が弱く、禁止・不可能の意を表す「長く保つべからず」とすべき。

issues.span: 金玉を満てた室は守れず
issues.advice: 原文は「金玉満堂」（金玉堂に満つ）で「室」ではない。「堂」と訳し、「金玉堂に満つれば、之を守る能わず」とすべき。

issues.span: 自棄にして咎を遺すなり
issues.advice: 「自遺其咎」は「自ら其の咎を遺す」。「自棄」は不要な付加で意味がずれるので削除し「自ら咎を遺す」と訳す。

issues.span: 持ちて満しむるは如し已に
issues.advice: 語順が破綻して読みにくい。「已むに如かず」と一続きに訳して文を整える。

payload.translation: 持ちて満しむるは如かず已むに、揣て鋭しむるは長保べからず、金玉を満てた堂を守れず、富貴を誇り自ら咎を遺すなり。功成名遂にして身退す。天の道なり。

issues.span: 金玉を満てた堂を守れず
issues.advice: The source says 金玉滿堂莫之能守 — 'gold and jade fill the hall, none can guard it.' The translation omits the subject of 'none can guard' and renders 滿堂 as '堂を満てた' modifying hall, losing the sense that no one can keep it. Render as 金玉堂に満つれども、之を守る能わず.

issues.span: 富貴を誇り自ら咎を遺すなり
issues.advice: Source is 富貴而驕自遺其咎 — 'wealth and honor with arrogance, one brings blame upon oneself.' 誇り (boast) is acceptable but 遺す should convey 'leave/bequeath to oneself' i.e. 自ら咎を遺す; acceptable but ensure 驕 (arrogance) is captured rather than mere boasting.

issues.span: 揣て鋭しむるは
issues.advice: 揣 is unusual; classical Japanese kanbun reading typically 揣 (はか)る. Consider 揣りて鋭しむる or 揣えて to be readable; current form is awkward.

issues.span: 持ちて満しむるは如かず已むに
issues.advice: Word order is strained; kanbun-style 持而盈之不如其已 reads better as 持ちて之を盈たすは已むに如かず. The object 之 is dropped.

issues.span: 長保べからず
issues.advice: 不可長保 = cannot be long preserved. 長保べからず is nonstandard; use 長く保つべからず.

payload.translation: 持ちて之を盈たすは已むに如かず、揣りて鋭しむるは長く保つべからず。金玉堂に満つれども、之を守る能わず。富貴を誇り、自ら咎を遺すなり。功成名遂にして身退す。天の道なり。

issues.span: 富貴を誇り、自ら咎を遺すなり
issues.advice: The source 富貴而驕 means 'to be rich and noble yet arrogant'; 誇り ('to boast') is a paraphrase. More importantly, the causal/logical link is lost: the arrogance is what brings the self-inflicted fault (自遺其咎). Render as '富貴にして驕れば、自ら其の咎を遺す' to preserve the conditional relation.

issues.span: 揣りて鋭しむるは
issues.advice: 揣 (chuǎi) here means 'to hammer/forge to a point' (as in 揣而銳之); 揣りて is an unusual reading. Consider a clearer rendering such as '鎚ちて之を鋭くするは' to convey the sense of sharpening/hammering.

issues.span: 持ちて之を盈たすは已むに如かず
issues.advice: Grammatically acceptable but stiff; 盈たす as a transitive with 之を is fine, though '盈たす' is rare. Could be smoothed, e.g. '持ちて之を盈たすは已むに如かず' is acceptable but consider '盈るる' vs. transitive clarity.

payload.translation: The ancient sages of the way were subtle, mysterious, and profound, yet beyond the grasp of the wise. For it is because they are beyond the grasp of the wise that they have assumed the form of the gentle and the easy. Like a traveler crossing a river in winter, they were cautious and wary of their neighbors. Like a guest, they were open and transparent, like ice about to melt, like the raw wood of a tree, like the valley of a stream, like the turbid water of a river. Who can make the turbid become still? Who can make the still become clear? Who can make the moving become still? Who can make the still become long-lasting? The one who holds this way does not desire to be full. For it is because they do not desire to be full that they can endure without change.

issues.span: beyond the grasp of the wise
issues.advice: 深不可識 means 'so deep as to be unknowable/inscrutable', not 'beyond the grasp of the wise'; remove the added 'of the wise'.

issues.span: they have assumed the form of the gentle and the easy
issues.advice: 彊為之容 means 'one is forced to describe their appearance'; it is not about assuming a form of gentleness.

issues.span: 豫若冬涉川
issues.advice: This describes hesitant caution like one crossing a frozen river in winter; 'gentle and the easy' and 'traveler' misrender 豫 (hesitant/cautious).

issues.span: 猶若畏四鄰
issues.advice: 猶若畏四鄰 means 'hesitant as if fearing neighboring states/enemies', not 'wary of their neighbors' in a social sense; also the parallel 豫/猶 structure is lost.

issues.span: 儼若客渙若冰將釋
issues.advice: 儼若客 = 'dignified/reverent like a guest'; 渙若冰將釋 = 'yielding/scattered like ice about to melt'. The translation merges these incorrectly ('open and transparent').

issues.span: 敦兮其若樸曠兮其若谷渾兮其若濁
issues.advice: These are three distinct similes: simple like uncarved wood, open/vast like a valley, murky like turbid water. The translation distorts them into 'raw wood of a tree', 'valley of a stream', 'turbid water of a river'.

issues.span: 孰能濁以靜之徐清孰能安以乆動之徐生
issues.advice: The two rhetorical questions are: 'Who can, from turbidity, by stillness, gradually clarify? Who can, from stability, by long movement, gradually generate life?' The translation splits into four questions and reverses the 靜/動 logic.

issues.span: 故能弊不新成
issues.advice: 弊不新成 means 'able to be worn out/old without needing new completion' — i.e., not requiring renewal. 'Endure without change' is inaccurate.

issues.span: 善為士者
issues.advice: 士 here is the adept/master of the Way; 'sages of the way' is acceptable but '善為士者' = 'those skilled in being a master/scholar' — render consistently as 'the adept'.

issues.span: Who can make the turbid become still? Who can make the still become clear? Who can make the moving become still? Who can make the still become long-lasting?
issues.advice: The four repetitive questions misrepresent the two-part parallel structure and read awkwardly; restore the 濁→靜→清 and 安→動→生 progression.

payload.translation: The adept of old, skillful in the Way, was subtle, mysterious, and profound, yet unknowable. For it is precisely because they are unknowable that they appear gentle and effortless. Like a traveler crossing a frozen river in winter, they were cautious and wary. Like a guest, they were dignified and reverent; like ice about to melt, like the open expanse of a valley, like the murky water of a stream. Who can turn the turbid into stillness? Who can turn stillness into clarity? Who can turn movement into stillness? Who can turn stillness into longevity? The one who holds this Way does not desire to be full. For it is because they do not desire to be full that they can endure without change.

issues.span: they appear gentle and effortless
issues.advice: 彊為之容 means 'forced to describe their appearance'; the translation renders it as 'gentle and effortless', which is a mistranslation of 彊為之容.

issues.span: Like a traveler crossing a frozen river in winter, they were cautious and wary
issues.advice: 豫若冬涉川猶若畏四鄰: 豫 (hesitant) and 猶 (cautious) are two separate similes; the translation merges them and adds 'frozen' (not in source) and omits the 畏四鄰 (fearing neighbors) image.

issues.span: like the open expanse of a valley, like the murky water of a stream
issues.advice: 敦兮其若樸曠兮其若谷渾兮其若濁: three similes (simple/uncarved, open/valley, murky/turbid) are compressed; 敦兮其若樸 (simple like uncarved wood) is omitted.

issues.span: Who can turn the turbid into stillness? Who can turn stillness into clarity? Who can turn movement into stillness? Who can turn stillness into longevity?
issues.advice: 孰能濁以靜之徐清孰能安以乆動之徐生: the source asks who can, being turbid, still it and gradually clarify; who can, being at rest, move it and gradually generate life. The translation reverses the causal direction and invents 'longevity'.

issues.span: they can endure without change
issues.advice: 故能弊不新成 means 'thus can be worn out without needing new completion/renovation'; 'endure without change' loses 弊 (worn/old) and 新成 (newly completed).

issues.span: the Way
issues.advice: 為士者 refers to the adept/scholar, not 'skillful in the Way'; 善為士者 means 'those good at being a true scholar/adept'. The rendering conflates 士 with 道.

issues.span: For it is precisely because they are unknowable that they appear gentle and effortless
issues.advice: The sentence is grammatically fine but the logic is distorted by the mistranslation; revise to reflect 'forced to describe their appearance'.

payload.translation: The adept of old, skillful in the Way, was subtle, mysterious, and profound, yet unknowable. For it is precisely because they are unknowable that they appear gentle and effortless. They were forced to describe their appearance, so they seemed hesitant and cautious, like a traveler crossing a frozen river in winter. They were dignified and reverent, like a guest. They were simple and uncarved, like a valley. They were murky and unrefined, like a stream. Who can turn the turbid into stillness? Who can turn stillness into clarity? Who can turn movement into stillness? Who can turn stillness into longevity? The one who holds this Way does not desire to be full. For it is because they do not desire to be full that they can endure without change.

issues.span: they appear gentle and effortless
issues.advice: The source '彊為之容' means 'one is forced to describe/characterize them'; the translation splits this into a separate sentence and misassigns 'appear gentle and effortless' — the '豫若冬涉川' simile (hesitant, like crossing a river in winter) is the actual description, not 'gentle and effortless'.

issues.span: like a traveler crossing a frozen river in winter
issues.advice: '涉川' means wading/crossing a river; 'frozen' is not in the source. Render as 'like one crossing a river in winter'.

issues.span: They were simple and uncarved, like a valley. They were murky and unrefined, like a stream.
issues.advice: The similes are misaligned: '敦兮其若樸' = simple/uncarved like raw wood (樸), '曠兮其若谷' = open/vast like a valley, '渾兮其若濁' = murky like turbid water. The translation drops '曠兮' (open/vast) and misassigns 'valley' to 'uncarved' and 'stream' to 'murky'.

issues.span: Who can turn the turbid into stillness? Who can turn stillness into clarity? Who can turn movement into stillness? Who can turn stillness into longevity?
issues.advice: The source is '孰能濁以靜之徐清，孰能安以乆動之徐生' — 'Who can, from turbidity, by stillness, gradually become clear? Who can, from stability, by prolonged movement, gradually come to life?' The translation inverts the causal relations and invents 'longevity'.

issues.span: they can endure without change
issues.advice: '能弊不新成' means 'can be worn/old without needing to be newly completed' — i.e., can remain imperfect and not require renewal. 'Endure without change' misses '不新成'.

issues.span: skillful in the Way
issues.advice: '善為士者' means 'those skilled as scholars/practitioners (士)', not 'skillful in the Way'; 士 is the person, not the Way.

issues.span: They were forced to describe their appearance, so they seemed hesitant
issues.advice: The causal 'so' is not in the source and creates a logical break; '彊為之容' introduces the following similes as a forced attempt at description.

payload.translation: 古に優れた者が、微妙玄通、深不可識の道を行く。そのようにして認識されないからこそ、強いて装い、容姿を豊かにし、安らぎを与えようとする。冬に川を渡るような、四隣を畏れ、客を待たせるように、氷を解き放つように、厚朴の素のようである。広く空しく谷のようである。混然として濁っているようである。誰が濁りを静かにし、徐々にして清らかにするだろうか。誰が動かし、徐々にして安らぎを与えようとするだろうか。この道を守り、これを満たさぬ者は、そのために不足を補う必要はない。なぜなら、満たさぬからこそ、弊を補うことができるからである。

issues.span: 古に優れた者が、微妙玄通、深不可識の道を行く
issues.advice: The source describes the ancient masters themselves as 微妙玄通深不可識 (subtle, mysterious, profound, penetrating, too deep to be recognized), not as walking a '道' of those qualities. Render the qualities as predicates of the person, not as a path.

issues.span: 強いて装い、容姿を豊かにし、安らぎを与えようとする
issues.advice: 彊為之容 means 'I will force myself to describe/sketch their appearance'; it is not about adorning or giving comfort. Convey the reluctant descriptive act.

issues.span: 客を待たせるように
issues.advice: 儼若客 means 'solemn/reverent as a guest'; 'making a guest wait' is a different meaning. Render as being dignified like a guest.

issues.span: 氷を解き放つように
issues.advice: 渙若冰將釋 means 'yielding/dissolving like ice about to melt'; 'releasing ice' misses the intransitive melting image.

issues.span: 厚朴の素のようである
issues.advice: 敦兮其若樸 means 'simple and unadorned like uncarved wood (樸)'; 厚朴 is a medicinal plant name and misreads 樸. Use the uncarved-wood image.

issues.span: 誰が動かし、徐々にして安らぎを与えようとするだろうか
issues.advice: 孰能安以乆動之徐生 means 'who can, being at rest, through prolonged movement bring about gradual life/growth?' The translation reverses the sense (movement producing rest) and omits 乆 (long/prolonged) and 生 (life).

issues.span: この道を守り、これを満たさぬ者は、そのために不足を補う必要はない
issues.advice: 保此道者不欲盈 means 'those who preserve this Way do not desire fullness/overflow'; it is not about not needing to make up for insufficiency. Render 不欲盈 as not seeking fullness.

issues.span: 弊を補うことができるからである
issues.advice: 夫惟不盈故能弊不新成 means 'precisely because one is not full, one can remain worn/old and not become newly completed/renovated' — i.e., can endure without needing renewal. '弊を補う' (make up for wornness) inverts the sense.

issues.span: 厚朴

issues.span: 微妙玄通、深不可識
issues.advice: These are descriptive predicates of the masters, not a proper name or path title; keep them as descriptive phrases rather than a nominalized '道'.

payload.translation: I am writing a biography of Ah Q, and it has been more than a couple of years. Yet, while I am writing, I am also constantly recalling it, which clearly shows that I am not a man of "establishing a name." For an immortal pen must be used by an immortal person, so people transmit through writing, and writing transmits through people. Ultimately, who transmits whom, has become increasingly unclear, and finally, it all boils down to transmitting Ah Q, as if there were ghosts in my thoughts.

issues.span: I am writing a biography of Ah Q, and it has been more than a couple of years
issues.advice: The source means the narrator has intended to write the biography for over a year or two (i.e., the intention has lasted that long), not that the writing is currently ongoing. Render as 'It has been more than a year or two since I wanted to write a biography of Ah Q.'

issues.span: while I am writing, I am also constantly recalling it
issues.advice: 『往回想』means to think back / reconsider / hesitate, not 'recalling it' (the biography). Convey the sense of second-guessing or turning things over in one's mind.

issues.span: a man of "establishing a name"
issues.advice: 『立言』is the classical Confucian virtue of 'establishing words/teachings that endure' (one of the three immortalities: 立德、立功、立言). Translate as 'a man who establishes enduring words' rather than 'establishing a name.'

issues.span: an immortal pen must be used by an immortal person
issues.advice: The source says an immortal pen must transmit/hand down an immortal person (须传不朽之人), i.e., the immortal brush must be devoted to immortalizing an immortal subject. The translation reverses the relation and drops 传.

issues.span: so people transmit through writing, and writing transmits through people
issues.advice: 『人以文传，文以人传』means a person is made known/transmitted through his writing, and the writing is transmitted through the person. 'People transmit through writing' is acceptable, but 'writing transmits through people' should be 'writing is handed down through the person'; clarify the reciprocal relation.

issues.span: it all boils down to transmitting Ah Q
issues.advice: 『归结到传阿Q』means it all comes down to writing Ah Q's biography (传 as 'to write a biography'), not 'transmitting Ah Q.' Use 'writing Ah Q's biography.'

issues.span: Ultimately, who transmits whom, has become increasingly unclear
issues.advice: Remove the comma after 'whom'; the clause reads awkwardly. Also 'who transmits whom' is vague—consider 'which depends on which.'

issues.span: as if there were ghosts in my thoughts
issues.advice: 『仿佛思想里有鬼似的』idiomatically means 'as if something were haunting my mind / as if a ghost were at work in my thoughts.' 'Ghosts in my thoughts' is understandable but loses the haunting nuance; consider 'as if a ghost were haunting my mind.'

payload.translation: Ah Q was not only his name and place of origin hazy; even his former deeds were hazy. issues.span: Ah Q was not only his name and place of origin hazy
issues.advice: The construction is garbled; the source means not only were his name and native place hazy, but also his past 'deeds/record' were hazy. Restructure so 'not only' governs the hazy name/origin clause.

issues.span: as long as he helped them, they would take him for a joke
issues.advice: The source says they only wanted him to help and only made fun of him (只要他帮忙，只拿他玩笑); the causal 'as long as...would' misrepresents the relationship. Render as two parallel facts: they only had him help and only made fun of him.

issues.span: Ah Q himself never spoke, but only when he argued with someone would he suddenly glare
issues.advice: The source says Ah Q himself also did not say (anything about it), and only occasionally (间或) when quarreling would he glare. 'Never spoke' is too absolute and 'suddenly' is not in the source; use 'did not speak of it himself' and 'occasionally'.

issues.span: deeds
issues.advice: '行状' is in scare quotes in the source, referring to his record/background; consider 'record' or 'exploits' to preserve the ironic quotation-marked term.

issues.span: only occasionally when he quarreled would he suddenly glare
issues.advice: '间或' modifies the occasional glaring during quarrels, not 'only occasionally'; adjust to reflect 'now and then, when quarreling, he would glare'.
